review.one_sentence_verdict: The manuscript now draws its claims narrowly enough to be defensible on a portfolio-average level, but the supported statement is so modest—'no material callable-interface residual on 18 pre-frozen DeepSeek endpoints at a prospectively chosen ±10-point margin with ~53% power'—that its methodological contribution is hard to separate from an appropriately cautious negative result.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Section 6.5 / Rsurf equivalence claim and Section 7 limitations on power
decision_critical_concerns.problem: The paper runs a TOST at ±10 points that passes (p=0.0121) but the authors' own parametric sensitivity calculation says only ~53% probability of declaring equivalence if the true mean is exactly zero. With n=18 endpoints, a 17.15-point endpoint SD, and a ±10-point margin, the TOST passing is largely driven by the wide margin and ceiling-heavy portfolio (where T−Rsurf is structurally zero). The 90% CI is [−5.6,5.6] and 95% CI is [−8.3,8.3], which barely fit inside ±10. This is not really an equivalence demonstration; it is a CI-contains-margin result under a generous, author-chosen threshold. The four strictly non-ceiling endpoints have residual mean 0 with [−25,25] interval, which is the only honest sub-population and it is completely unresolved.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: The headline 'equivalence at the frozen material margin' is doing more rhetorical work than the numbers support. A reader who sees TOST p<0.05 will likely interpret this as 'we have shown the callable surface does not matter.' The manuscript must either (a) recharacterize the result as 'the data are consistent with equivalence at ±10pp on the registered portfolio, with low power and a ceiling-dominated sample' or (b) make the claim tighter by either reducing the margin or expanding n. As stated, the abstract's 'exact-output context-materialization control supports equivalence' is the kind of phrasing reviewers should flag.
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: Recharacterization alone would move the paper from borderline to weak_accept, because the methodological audit contribution (decomposition + verdict-reversal demo + surface-control) would stand on a properly caveated equivalence statement rather than an overclaimed one.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Section 6.2 EIA classification and Section 6.4 'compatibility-selected mechanism replication'
decision_critical_concerns.problem: The manuscript honestly classifies EIA as 'compatibility-selected post-review' and 'net repair with surface interaction.' But then it also reports T−N=+37.5, p=0.031 (one-sided exact sign test, n=8), and uses this as the primary empirical demonstration that net repair is preserved under stronger controls. The arithmetic is internal-consistent: +62.5−25=+37.5. But the contrast is doing two jobs—it is the cell that shows the surface interaction classification working, and it is also the cell that supplies the headline net-repair p-value. A reader who accepts the surface-interaction downgrade will, fairly, ask why EIA should be the load-bearing net-repair cell. The fresh DeepSeek C3/C4 grounding cells (T−N=+30, +20) have n=5 and bootstrap intervals that include zero, so they cannot independently carry the claim. The net result is that the net-repair claim rests almost entirely on a cell the authors simultaneously flag as confounded.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: This is the most important internal tension in the paper. The honest framing in 6.4 says EIA is not confirmatory; the empirical emphasis in the abstract says EIA is 'a compatibility-selected EIA mechanism replication shows a net T−N repair of +37.5 points.' The 'shows' language is at odds with the disclaimers. Either EIA is evidence of net repair (and the surface-interaction caveat is a secondary qualifier) or EIA is a proof-of-existence case (and the net-repair p-value should not headline the empirical contribution).
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: A clean separation—'EIA demonstrates the audit contract in a confounded cell; net-repair evidence comes from the fresh DeepSeek C3/C4 grounding, which is directional only on n=5'—would resolve the tension and let the methodological contribution carry the paper without leaning on a downgraded cell.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Section 4.1 base N/G/T and the G 'target-blind' matching claim
decision_critical_concerns.problem: The argument for why T−G is meaningful hinges on G being 'complexity-matched' (equal lexical-token and AST-node count) and 'target-blind' (cannot perform the registered temporal operation). But the G helpers in Appendix A are not truly blind to the target operation—G1 still filters evidence by a schema_ceiling string, G2 still extracts a regex match, G3 still filters spans by a list of markers. They differ from T only in which key/pattern they inspect. The DeepSeek C3 cutoff false positive in 6.1 is then explained as 'G degrades N' because G1 is misaligned to the task, not because G is benign-but-non-targeted. This is a substantive modeling choice that the paper does not defend: if G and T are equally specific to different task-relevant keys, T−G is a within-family refactor comparison, not a 'no-operation generic helper' comparison. The reviewer cannot tell whether G was designed to be a useful foil or a deliberately weak strawman.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: If the G construction is stronger than described, T−G is meaningful but harder to achieve; if it is weaker than described, the +28-point false positive in 6.1 is partly a result of G underperforming on a task it was nominally built for. Either way, the paper needs an explicit justification of why the matching procedure is a fair test of the 'targeted-versus-generic' hypothesis, including a sensitivity check where G uses a different but plausible key.
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: A one-paragraph defense plus a sensitivity computation (e.g., G using a different but plausible filter key on C3 cutoff) would neutralize this concern. Without it, the central illustration (the false positive) is interpretable as a design artifact.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Section 2/4.3 Rsurf as a 'callable-interface' test and the persistent claim that Rsurf 'reuses T's exact operation output'
decision_critical_concerns.problem: The claim that Rsurf tests 'callable-interface value' is conceptually fragile. Rsurf takes the byte-identical T output and materializes it inside the context, then exposes no callable helper. But under a forced one-answer harness, the only thing a callable interface can do that materialized context cannot is allow the model to call the helper during generation rather than seeing its output up front. The Rsurf design collapses this to a no-op by construction: the model never gets to call anything in Rsurf, but it also never gets to call anything in T that affects the final answer (because T's output is a single-shot retrieval operation that the harness uses to filter evidence before generation). If neither arm allows mid-generation helper calls, the 'callable interface' is functionally identical in both arms except for the surface of the same object. The paper acknowledges this in 4.3 ('forced one-answer harness') but does not grapple with the implication: the test shows that the harness surface does not matter under this harness, which is not the same as showing the callable interface does not matter in deployment.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: The conclusion in Section 8 says 'use T−Rsurf for callable-interface value when operation content is exactly matched.' But under the frozen harness, callable-interface value is a property of multi-turn/interactive deployments, which the Rsurf design explicitly does not test. A reader who applies this audit in a different harness will draw the wrong inference. This is not a claim the paper makes (it disclaims multi-turn equivalence), so it is major rather than critical—but the audit's 'recipe' framing in the conclusion oversells what Rsurf actually tests.
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: Replace 'callable-interface value' with 'surface-isolation value under a forced one-answer harness' in the recipe and abstract, and note explicitly that multi-turn and interactive use cases require a different control. This is a wording fix, but it changes what the paper claims its audit contract can be used for.

noncritical_repairs: The abstract says 'across 18 pre-frozen DeepSeek endpoints T−Rsurf is 0.0 points'—consider reporting the 95% CI alongside the point estimate in the abstract so the reader does not have to infer it.

Section 6.2 reports 'fresh two-repeat tranche' results for DeepSeek C3/C4 grounding but does not say whether these endpoints overlap with the 18-endpoint Rsurf portfolio. Make the endpoint set relationships explicit across all sections.
The parametric sensitivity calculation of ~53% is described but not labeled as a post-hoc power analysis. Move it into a labeled subsection so reviewers do not have to infer its role.
Table 2 reports confidence intervals as [95%] but the abstract and main text mostly use 90% intervals; unify the interval level or explicitly say which is the registered level.

The 'Kimi alignment check is consistent with that narrow surface result: on three held-out endpoints, T and Rsurf both succeed on all five fresh repeats' is a one-sentence support that adds no information—either expand it with intervals or remove it.

In Section 4.2, the sentence 'We do not label G0 behaviorally neutral at the stratum level' is good but Section 5.2 still uses 'same-surface no-operation placebo' in a way that could be read as neutrality. Tighten the terminology.
claims_to_downgrade_or_delete: Delete or substantially downgrade the phrase 'supports equivalence' in the abstract. Replace with 'is consistent with portfolio-average equivalence at a prospectively frozen ±10-point margin under low power.'

Downgrade 'an exact-output context-materialization control supports equivalence' to 'a TOST at the frozen ±10-point margin passes, but the design is not high-powered and the non-ceiling subset is unresolved.'

Remove the unqualified 'shows a net T−N repair of +37.5 points' from the abstract EIA sentence; instead write 'on a compatibility-selected cell where G0−N=−25, T−N is +37.5 points; we retain the net-repair claim but flag the surface interaction.'

Section 8 conclusion: 'support portfolio-level surface equivalence at the frozen margin' should be 'is consistent with portfolio-level surface equivalence at the frozen margin; the supported statement does not generalize to non-ceiling strata, multi-turn settings, or independently designed temporal retrievers.'
evidence_that_is_now_convincing: The DeepSeek C3-R cutoff false-positive demonstration (T=100, G=72, N=100, hence T−N=0) is clean, well-controlled, and the kind of result that should have been in the evaluation literature earlier.

The contrast decomposition T−N = (T−G0) + (G0−N) is correctly stated as a decomposition of contrasts and not a mediation theorem, and the paper correctly refuses to call T−G0 a 'pure operation effect' when G0−N ≠ 0. This is the central methodological move and it is now defensible.

The honest classification of EIA as 'compatibility-selected post-review' and the resulting refusal to treat it as confirmatory cross-domain evidence is exactly what the prior reviewer panel asked for.
The prospective freezing of the ±10-point Rsurf margin before outcomes, combined with reporting both preregistered and post-hoc interval levels, is appropriate transparency for a frozen audit.
The Rsurf zero-call parity audit (hash match, evidence-package recovery, no candidate reordering) is the right kind of control to isolate the integration surface.
The explicit parametric sensitivity estimate (~53%) and the explicit 'we do not describe the design as high-powered' statement prevent the TOST from being overread by a careful reader.
review.novelty_boundary: The novelty is methodological and lives entirely in the audit contract: a four-contrast decomposition (T−N, T−G0, G0−N, T−Rsurf) with a prospective threshold for the surface-isolation test, applied to a small source-native endpoint portfolio. The paper does not claim novelty in procedure reuse, time-aware retrieval, or paired skill causality, and the related-work section is appropriately modest. The novelty boundary is real but thin: any future paper that applies the same decomposition to a different skill family or a larger endpoint set subsumes this work as a special case. The current paper's residual contribution is the demonstration that the audit changes verdicts, which is genuine even if the scale is small.
review.single_highest_value_next_action: Recharacterize the Rsurf equivalence claim in the abstract, Section 6.5, and Section 8 as 'consistent with portfolio-average equivalence at a prospectively frozen ±10-point margin under a low-power design with a ceiling-heavy sample, with the strictly non-ceiling subset left unresolved'—and separate the EIA empirical contribution cleanly from the EIA classification discussion so that the net-repair p-value does not rest on the cell that the audit simultaneously flags as confounded. No new experiment is needed for the current narrow claim; the fix is in how the existing numbers are described and weighted.
